issue_context.title: WebApplicationBuilder.WebHost.UseWebRoot(string) throws given a relative path
issue_context.body:
```C#
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.WebHost.UseWebRoot("www");
```

```
> dotnet run
Building...
Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentException: The path must be absolute. (Parameter 'root')
   at Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.PhysicalFileProvider..ctor(String root, ExclusionFilters filters) in Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Physical.dll:token 0x600001b+0x28
   at Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.PhysicalFileProvider..ctor(String root) in Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Physical.dll:token 0x600001a+0x0
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder.WebHostEnvironment.ResolveFileProviders(IConfiguration configuration) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.dll:token 0x6000071+0x19
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder.ConfigureWebHostBuilder.UseSetting(String key, String value) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.dll:token 0x600003c+0x91
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.HostingAbstractionsWebHostBuilderExtensions.UseWebRoot(IWebHostBuilder hostBuilder, String webRoot) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Abstractions.dll:token 0x600000d+0xe
   at <Program>$.<Main>$(String[] args) in C:\dev\halter73\swagger\Minimal\Program.cs:line 6
```


On a "real" `IWebHostBuilder`, relative paths are supported and appear to be treated relative to the `I(Web)HostEnvironment.ContentRootPath`.

**Note**: No ArgumentException is only thrown if a `www` exists in the current working directory because of [this check](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/e858e3dabbe8b9e0cbd8b6f57fcd7a5652984252/src/DefaultBuilder/src/WebHostEnvironment.cs#L98-L101). Both the `Directory.Exists` check and `PhysicalFileProvider` should work on the same normalized path.
comments: Until preview7, you can use something like `Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "www")` to work around this issue.

review_comments: Can we add a WebApplicationFunctionalTests that checks we have a working PhysicalFileProvider too?
This is validated in `WebHostEnvironmentTests.SettingPathsSetsContentProviders` now. Not a full end-to-end test but validates that the providers are updated when the path is.
Can we verify that the PhysicalFileProviders have the correct `Root` in this test too?

I changed my mind about this. I think we do need to preserve the relative web root path and re-ResolvePathToRoot when the ContentRootPath changes in order to keep the behavior consistent with the generic host when you call UseWebRoot() before UseContentRoot().
Shouldn't we have logic like what you pointed to in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/34140#discussion_r664953734 to handle a relative content root path?
